title: Retained localization does not enlarge the principal w-localization
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $T\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$ a closed subset. For the retained localization $R_{[T]}$ of [def-weil-pbc-retained-localization], $|R_{[T]}|\leq|R^w|$, where $R^w$ is [def-weil-pbc-w-localization]. No infinitude hypothesis on either ring is needed.

source.place: Tag 0984 (remark-size-w-contractible), first three stages and the localization estimate for C; blueprint sec-proper-base-change/sk-thm-properbasechange/lem-weil-pbc-retained-localization.md, proof first paragraph (retained localization as an idempotent quotient).

proof.text: Each selector e_E of [def-weil-pbc-retained-localization] is idempotent. Mathlib IsLocalization.Away.algebraMap_surjective_of_isIdempotentElem proves that R^w → (R^w)[1/e_E] is surjective: for a fraction a/e_E^n, the idempotent e_E becomes one after localization, so the fraction is the image of a.

The neighbourhood category is filtered by its defining theorem. Every element of its colimit is the image of an element of one localization by the representative clause of [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise], transferred through the preserved filtered colimit of CommAlgCat. Step 1 lifts that element to b in R^w. Since the stage inclusion is an R^w-algebra homomorphism, its image of the structural image of b is exactly algebraMap b. Therefore R^w → R_[T] is surjective. Cardinal.mk_le_of_surjective yields the claimed inequality. This argument also covers T empty, T the whole spectrum, and a zero ring R.
